desc: Base the next PCIe candidate on UPSTREAM's merged t8132/t6040 support instead of our diverged fork. Verified in upstream/main src/pcie.c: APCIE_PHY_CTRL_RESET_T8132=BIT(4), 'apcie,t6040' matches regs_t8132 (PR 633, merged) — INDEPENDENT CONFIRMATION of today's delta D2, which our own NEXT_STEPS ticket-046 audit had ALREADY recorded upstream and we never applied (our fork cleared BIT(7) through every op-115 run). Our fork is 13 behind / 94 ahead. Upstream LACKS: our ticket-058 clkgen PLL enable+lock (proven to lock) and delta D1 clkgen[0]|=BIT(5). Upstream HAS: GXF guarded-stack fix 2ea75b66 (relevant to our GENTER hang — our GXF experiments predate it), ATC LN0/LN1_RX_TOP_USB_EQA offsets 639e0506, and no diagnostic early-returns. PLAN: candidate = upstream t8132 path + our clkgen sequence + D1, scaffolding dropped. HYPOTHESIS THIS TESTS: upstream reportedly reaches link-up on plain M4 with NO clkgen work, so op-115 may have been the reset-bit error alone and our clkgen sequence may not be a precondition. CAVEATS: upstream validated on t8132 (M4, J773g) not t6040 (M4 Pro, more CIO3/PCIe blocks); no early return means a boot runs the full PHY+port sequence, so ATTENDED either way. Supersedes the approach of patching our fork (19edc72b stays as the decode record).
author: claude

Cross-agent exact-artifact review still required before either boots. NOTE this candidate IS observable over a caught gadget window (m1n1's boot log reaches run_actions/usb_init), unlike the R3 experiment. | 2026-07-29 ATTENDED — OP-115 SOLVED (evidence/2026-07-29-t6040-pcie-op115-SOLVED-links-dont-train.md). V1 (upstream PCIe wholesale, 28a4e0cf) chainloaded over KIS; PCIe triggered on demand via the proxy P_PCIE_INIT command (p.pcie_init(), no kernel payload). pcie_init COMPLETED for the first time on T6040: 'Initializing t6040 PCIe controller' / port 0 + port 1 max speed 2 / 'Initialized controller 0' / returned 0. CONFIRMED: the wrong PHY reset bit (BIT(7) vs BIT(4)) was the ENTIRE cause — our ticket-058 clkgen PLL sequence and delta D1 were NOT preconditions, so V2 (3916bf15) is UNNECESSARY, do not run it. Linux then booted with the PCIe DT (Image-pcie + t6040-j614s-dcuart-pcie.dtb) to a BusyBox shell: pcie-apple probes, ECAM at 0x1cb0000000 for bus 00-08, both root ports enumerate (0000:00:00.0 and 00:01.0, 106b:100c, PME+AER on IRQ 52/54). REMAINING BLOCKER = LINK TRAINING: 'pci@0,0 link didn't come up' + 'pci@1,0 link didn't come up', and DLL_LINK_ACTIVE=0 read independently from m1n1 over the proxy (LnkCap 0x00737812 max gen2 x1, LnkSta 0x1011 on both ports). No BCM4388, no SD reader. RULED OUT: PERST pins correct (ADT function-perst GPIO 0x4/0x5 == our reset-gpios 4/5); CLKREQ pinmux present and referenced (ADT function-clkreq GPIO(0,2)/(1,2) == our pcie-pins pinmux 0x20000/0x20001 via pinctrl-0); PINCTRL_APPLE_GPIO=y and 51c000000.pinctrl bound; DT reg layout correct (ECAM+rc+4 port core+4 port phy); no PCIe dmesg errors beyond the two link lines (pms_fpwm/HID errors are pre-existing and unrelated); double-init is NOT the cause of no-link (m1n1 alone on a virgin boot also shows DLL_LINK_ACTIVE=0). NOTE m1n1's Apple port checks (APCIE_PORT_STATUS_RUN/LINKSTS) pass silently and are NOT equivalent to DLL_LINK_ACTIVE — 'Initialized controller 0' does not mean link up. HAZARD FOUND: pcie_init must run ONCE PER POWER CYCLE. Running it from the proxy and then again from kboot caused a synchronous data abort (ESR 0x96000410, FAR 0x41705a000 = port 2 PHY-IP window +0x2000) and a reboot; the clean-boot retry worked. The pcie_initialized static guards only within one m1n1 instance, not across a chainload. NEXT (priority order): (1) endpoint POWER — ADT pci-bridge1 has function-sd_pwr_en = SMC key 'gP19' so the SD reader cannot train without an SMC key write (a NEW SMC write beyond smc_reboot/smc_rtc: needs decode + explicit approval); pci-bridge0 (WiFi) has NO pwren in the ADT so its rail comes from elsewhere — identify it. (2) ADT per-bridge timing t-refclk-to-perst=100 / perst-to-config=100 — check pcie-apple honours an equivalent delay on t602x. (3) 'no iommu-map translation for id 0x0/0x8' in dmesg. (4) diff yuka's t8140-pcie (a7857af8) port bring-up for anything M4-specific after LTSSM start.
